name: webpack-config-require-in-callback
hook: require works inside webpack config callbacks even when next.config.js is ESM
body: Webpack config callbacks (the function passed to webpack:) run in Node.js at build time, not at config-file-load time. This means `require` is available inside the callback even when next.config.js uses ESM imports at the top level. This allows accessing Next.js's bundled webpack modules via `require('next/dist/compiled/webpack/webpack.js')` from inside the callback.
why: Next.js 15's next.config.js is ESM at the top level, but webpack bundling happens at runtime in Node.js. The callback is evaluated by Node.js directly, not by an ESM module loader. This is the bridge between the ESM config file and CommonJS webpack internals.

name: normalmodulereplacementplugin-tap-error
hook: NormalModuleReplacementPlugin from Next.js bundled webpack causes tap undefined error in Next.js 15.5.9
body: Using `require('next/dist/compiled/webpack/webpack.js')` + `init()` + `NormalModuleReplacementPlugin` inside the webpack config callback causes `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'tap')` during the webpack build in Next.js 15.5.9. The plugin creates successfully but triggers a tap error during compilation. The fix is to NOT use NormalModuleReplacementPlugin — webpack 5 handles node: protocol imports natively when packages are in serverExternalPackages.
why: The NormalModuleReplacementPlugin approach was tried to handle node: protocol imports (node:crypto, node:fs) but caused a webpack plugin error during the build minification phase. Since all problematic packages (like @napi-rs/canvas) are already in serverExternalPackages, webpack never processes their node: imports in the browser bundle. The dev branch has no node: protocol handling and builds fine.

name: resolve-alias-cannot-intercept-node-protocol
hook: resolve.alias cannot intercept node: URL scheme imports
body: webpack resolve.alias uses exact string matching (or $ suffix for exact match), but it does NOT interpret regex patterns. A key like '^node:' or '\.node$' in resolve.alias will match literal module names, not node: URL scheme imports. The '\.node$' pattern only matches file paths ending in .node, not the node: protocol.
why: The `node:` protocol is a separate resolution path in webpack 5 from module name resolution. resolve.alias operates on module names, not URL schemes. Only a ResolvePlugin can intercept the full request string including the protocol, but NormalModuleReplacementPlugin causes the tap error.
